gamma_events.title: Highest temperature in Munich on August 21?
gamma_events.description:
This market will resolve based on the highest temperature recorded in the 'Daily Observations' table on Weather Underground, not the figure displayed in the 'Day High & Low' summary section; in the event of any discrepancy between the two, the Daily Observations table shall be the primary resolution source not the Day High & Low section.

This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded at the Munich Airport Station in degrees Celsius on 21 Aug '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from Wunderground, specifically the highest temperature recorded for all times on this day for the Munich Airport Station, available here: https://www.wunderground.com/history/daily/de/munich/EDDM.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the gear icon next to the search bar and switch the Temperature setting between °F and °C.

This market can not resolve until the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description: Persistent cloud cover, widespread showers, and afternoon thunderstorms driven by a moist, unstable air mass are capping solar insolation and limiting daytime heating across Munich on August 21. Official forecasts from multiple sources converge on a maximum of 20–23 °C, well below the long-term average high of ~24 °C, as northeasterly to northwesterly flow advects cooler maritime air and enhances evaporative cooling from heavy precipitation. Small differences among leading market outcomes (21–23 °C) hinge on the precise timing and intensity of convective cells: earlier or more intense rain suppresses the peak by an additional 1–2 °C, while brief breaks in cloud cover could allow marginal warming toward the upper end of the range. Updated model runs and surface observations through the afternoon will be the key catalysts for any late shifts in trader sentiment.

This aligns with National Weather Service model guidance and falls near the 1991–2020 climatological average high of 82.7°F, with no strong warm advection or clear-sky conditions to push readings higher. Trader consensus at 100% for the 84–85°F bin reflects convergence across official preliminary climatological data (CF6 reports) and real-time ASOS measurements. An unlikely upward revision from station-specific microclimates or post-processed quality control could theoretically shift the outcome, though current data alignment makes such changes improbable before market resolution.

eventMetadata.context_description:
**Forecasts for Munich on August 22, 2026, center on a maximum of 20–23 °C under broken clouds and scattered showers, producing the tight clustering of market probabilities around 21 °C (36.5 %), 22 °C (27.0 %), and 20 °C (19.5 %).**

Official guidance from the Met Office, BBC, AccuWeather, and timeanddate.com converges on daytime highs near 21–22 °C (roughly 70 °F), with passing showers or thundery activity expected to reduce insolation and cap afternoon warming. Recent model runs highlight a transient Atlantic front or upper-level trough increasing cloud cover and precipitation chances, which historically suppresses peak temperatures by 2–4 °C relative to clear-sky climatology for late August (long-term average highs near 22–23 °C). 

Wind direction (southwesterly to westerly, 7–10 mph) and surface moisture from overnight lows in the low teens °C further limit boundary-layer heating. Traders therefore assign the highest implied probabilities to the narrow 20–22 °C band, reflecting both the consensus forecast and residual uncertainty over exact shower timing and any late-day clearing that could allow a brief spike toward 23 °C. Updated NWP guidance and radar trends through the evening of August 21 will be the key near-term catalysts.
